'''R. J. Dwayne Miller''' {{Post-nominals|country=CAN|FRSC|MCIC|FRS}} is a [[Canadians|Canadian]] [[chemist]] and a professor at the [[University of Toronto]]. His focus is in [[physical chemistry]] and [[biophysics]]. He is most widely known for his work in [[ultrashort pulse|ultrafast]] [[laser science]], [[time-resolved spectroscopy]], and 
the development of new [[femtosecond]] [[electron diffraction|electron sources]] that facilitates [[ultrafast electron diffraction]] experiments. His research has enabled real-time observation of atomic motions in materials during chemical processes and has shed light on the structure-function correlation that underlies biology.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.cifar.ca/profiles/r-j-dwayne-miller/ | title=R. J. Dwayne Miller | access-date=5 October 2017 | website=Canadian Institute for Advanced Research}}</ref>

==Early life and education==

Miller was born and raised in [[Winnipeg]], Manitoba.<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.winnipegfreepress.com/local/Winnipeg-chemist-earns-prestigious-British-science-award-378588676.html | title=Winnipeg chemist earns prestigious British science award | access-date=5 October 2017| newspaper=Winnipeg Free Press | date=2016-05-09 | last1=Paul | first1=Alexandra }}</ref> In 1978, he received a [[Bachelor of Science|B.Sc.]] in chemistry and [[immunology]] at the [[University of Manitoba]] where Bryan R. Henry was his advisor. He completed his [[doctor of philosophy|Ph.D.]] in chemistry at [[Stanford University]] in 1983 under the supervision of [[Michael D. Fayer]]. His thesis work focused on energy transport in model systems of [[photosynthesis]] and is titled ''Part I, Electronic excited state transport and trapping in disordered systems; Part II, Laser induced ultrasonics''.

==Academic career==

Following graduation, Miller gained a faculty position at the [[University of Rochester]] and immediately took a 12-month leave to do [[Postdoctoral researcher|postdoctoral research]] in solid state physics as a [[NATO]] science fellow at the Laboratoire de Spectrometrie Physique (renamed to Laboratoire Interdisciplinaire de Physique in 2011<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www-liphy.ujf-grenoble.fr/History-of-LiPhy?lang=en/ | title=History of LiPhy | access-date=6 October 2017 | website=Laboratoire Interdisciplinaire de Physique}}</ref>) at the [[Joseph Fourier University|Université Joseph Fourier]] in [[Grenoble]], [[France]] under the direction of Hans Peter Trommsdorff and Robert Romenstain.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://lphys.chem.utoronto.ca/members/resources/dwayne-miller-cv | title=R. J. Dwayne Miller | access-date=5 October 2017 | website=Miller Group}}</ref>
He returned to University of Rochester in 1984 as an [[assistant professor]] of chemistry. He was promoted to [[associate professor]] in 1988 and then full [[professor]] of chemistry and [[optics]] in 1992. In 1995, he moved back to [[Canada]] and relocated his research group to the departments of chemistry and physics at the University of Toronto. In 2006, he was appointed as a University Professor <ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.provost.utoronto.ca/awards/uprofessors/complete/dmiller.htm/ | title=Professor RJ Dwayne Miller | access-date=5 October 2017 | website=University of Toronto}}</ref> and later as a Distinguished Faculty Research Chair.

From 2010-2014, R. J. D. Miller was the director of the Max Planck Group, Centre for Free Electron Laser Science/DESY, University of Hamburg. From 2014-2020, he was the co-founding director of [[List of Max Planck Institutes|Max Planck Institute for the Structure and Dynamics of Matter (MPSD)]] in [[Hamburg]], [[Germany]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Prof. Dr. R. J. Dwayne Miller |url=http://www.mpsd.mpg.de/person/32916/7437/ |access-date=5 October 2017 |website=Max Planck Institute for the Structure and Dynamics of Matter}}</ref>

In 2023, he was inducted as a fellow of the [[Royal Society]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dwayne Miller |url=https://royalsociety.org/people/dwayne-miller-36204/ |access-date=2023-05-26 |website=royalsociety.org}}</ref> and has been a fellow of [[Royal Society of Canada]] and the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]] since 1999 and 2016, respectively. He is also a member of the [[Chemical Institute of Canada]], [[Canadian Association of Physicists]], [[American Physical Society]], and [[Optical Society of America]].

==Science outreach==

Beyond his scientific work, Miller is dedicated to the promotion of science education through outreach to school children. He founded and is a board member of [[Science Rendezvous]], an annual [[science festival]] that aims to expose general public to science and technology.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.sciencerendezvous.ca/ | title=Prof. Dr. R. J. Dwayne Miller | access-date=5 October 2017 | website=Science Rendezvous}}</ref>
